newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatist says Paris in deal with rival.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatist says Paris in deal with rival.

text.p: A Corsican separatist leader accused the French government and a rival group on Wednesday of working together to discredit his own organisation.

In the latest episode in a long-simmering feud between rival separatist movements, Alain Orsoni, head of the Movement for Self-Determination (MPA), accused the government and the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) "historic wing" of conspiring together to blame it wrongly for a car bomb attack.
Fifteen MPA members were arrested on Sunday and Monday over a car-bomb attack in the port of Bastia in July which killed a member of the "historic wing". Seven were released on Wednesday.
Orsoni said "historic wing" leader Francois Santoni, who is on the run from French police, had agreed to work with the French authorities in order to get rid of the MPA.
The MPA is the legal front for the FLNC's "traditional wing" which is involved in a factional battle with the historic wing over strategy in their fight for independence from mainland France.

"We can say that the FLNC historic wing is making a new kind of deal with the government, which is: liquidate the MPA and we won't explode any more bombs in France," Orsoni told a news conference on the Mediterranean resort island.
"Taking apart rival organisations is one of the stated aims of the FLNC historic wing," he said.
The government regularly cracks down on the FLNC historic wing which is responsible for most bombings on mainland France and in Corsica.

The most recent attack by the historic wing was the bombing on Monday of the post office in the southern mainland city of Aix-en-Provence a few hours before French President Jacques Chirac was to meet Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar in nearby Marseille.
The historic wing also claimed responsibility for the October 5 bombing of the city hall in the southwestern city of Bordeaux, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe serves as mayor.
